A.why: The supply voltage is calculated as V = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2) = sqrt(40^2 + (60 - 30)^2) = 50 V.

B.why: 70 V is the arithmetic sum of V_R and (V_L - V_C), not the phasor sum.

C.why: 130 V is the simple scalar sum of all voltages (60 + 30 + 40), which ignores phase differences.

D.why: 10 V is incorrect because voltages in an AC circuit add as vectors, resulting in 50 V.
